articles.title: Bengaluru Metro Phase 3 Work Begins: BMRCL Floats Tenders to Demolish Buildings
articles.description: Bengaluru's Metro Phase 3 is advancing into a preparatory stage, with the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) issuing tenders for building demolition. This groundwork is essential to clear land for the new metro corridors, including routes from JP Nagar 4th Phase to Mysore Road and Hosahalli to Kadabagere.

articles.title: Mismanagement, irregularities cost Tamil Nadu PSUs Rs 3,299 crore: CAG
articles.description: Widespread financial mismanagement, tender irregularities and governance deficits across Tamil Nadu's State Public Sector Enterprises resulted in compliance-related financial implications of Rs 3,298.75 crore, a CAG report has revealed.

articles.title: Lot-I tender first step towards Rs 35,000 Cr project: MLA Ramban
articles.description: Ramban MLA Arjun Singh Raju on Wednesday said the opening of the technical bid for Lot-I of the much-awaited project would mark an important first step towards its implementation, while clarifying that the Lot-I tender should not be confused with the main project. Speaking to reporters, Raju said the technical bid for Lot-I, involving works worth around Rs 5,000 Cr, was expected to be opened on Wednesday. He said the financial bid would be processed after completion of the technical evaluation, following which the work under Stage-I, Lot-I, would be allotted and taken up. The MLA said the project had witnessed repeated delays over the past several years due to a number of pending issues, including matters related to land possession. He said these issues had also affected the progress of the Lot-I tender. According to Raju, the overall project is estimated to cost around Rs 35,000 Cr, with the government having approved subordinate debt of approximately Rs 18,000 Cr for NHPC at a relatively low rate of interest. He further said the proposal for the main project was presently awaiting consideration by the Public Investment Board, which examines major projects of the Central Government and public sector undertakings on various parameters, including financial viability and cost-effectiveness. “I expect the Public Investment Board to clear the proposal by the end of October,” Raju said, adding that after the required approvals, including Cabinet approval, the main project tenders would be floated and work on the main project could commence. The MLA also urged people not to link the Lot-I tender with the entire project, saying that Lot-I represented an initial stage and would enable work worth more than Rs 5,000 Cr to begin. He said the development was a positive step after years of uncertainty and would provide momentum to the overall project. “Lot-I is an important beginning, but the main project will still require some more time and the necessary approvals,” Raju said.

articles.title: 5 firms submit bids for Sawalkot Hydroelectric Project
articles.description: The tendering process for Lot-I of the Sawalkot Hydroelectric Project (HEP) in Jammu and Kashmir) has moved forward with five major infrastructure companies submitting bids for the package. The technical bids for Lot-I of the proposed 1,800-MW Sawalkot Hydroelectric Project were opened on Wednesday, marking a significant step forward in the long-pending project. According to the Government e-Procurement System, the technical bids for Lot-I were opened by the duly constituted Tender Opening Committee (TOC). The five bidders include Adani Infra India Ltd, Hindustan Construction Co Ltd, Larsen and Toubro Ltd, Patel Engineering Ltd, and Rithwik Projects Pvt Ltd. All five bids have been admitted under the fee, pre-qualification and technical categories. The tender has been floated by NHPC Limited, Corporate Office, Faridabad, under Tender ID 2026_NHPC_8906835_1, with the tender reference number NH/CCW/CC-III/CO439/PRI 4325/91. The e-procurement tender summary report, updated on September 9, stated that the technical bids of all five bidders had been opened by the duly constituted TOC. The development marks a significant step forward in the tendering process for the long-awaited Sawalkot HEP project. The opening of the technical bids will now pave the way for scrutiny and evaluation of the bidders' technical and eligibility documents before the tendering process proceeds to the subsequent stages. The Sawalkot Hydroelectric Project is among the major proposed power projects in the Chenab basin and has remained a subject of considerable public and political interest, particularly over delays in taking the project forward. Welcoming the development, president of the Sawalkote Joint Action Committee (SJAC), advocate Fairoz Khan, congratulated the people of Ramban and members of the committee for their continued efforts and support for the project-related issues. Khan said the opening of the technical bids was an important development, but stressed that the tendering process should now proceed without further delay and the government should announce a firm timeline for execution of the project. He reiterated that the SJAC was not opposed to development or nation-building, but wanted the rights and interests of the people affected by the project to be protected. He pointed out that nearly 88 per cent of the project’s submergence area falls in Ramban district, making local participation and adequate safeguards particularly important. The SJAC president demanded fair and timely compensation to all affected landowners in accordance with the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013. He also sought first preference for local youth of Ramban in project-related employment, contracts and services, besides a comprehensive rehabilitation and resettlement package for displaced families, including livelihood and wage security. Khan further called for clarity on road connectivity and diversion plans, saying there should be transparent communication regarding infrastructure that would be affected by the project. He also demanded a review of land acquired earlier but remaining unused, with such land either returned to the owners or compensated afresh as per law. The SJAC also stressed the need for adequate environmental and social safeguards to ensure that the project does not adversely affect local ecology and communities. “We are ready for dialogue, but we will not accept empty promises,” Khan said, asserting that Ramban should be treated as a stakeholder and not a sacrifice zone. He said the SJAC would continue to pursue its demands through peaceful and legal means and would remain engaged with the government and project authorities to safeguard the interests of the people of Ramban. “Ramban is not a sacrifice zone; it is a stakeholder, and its people deserve their rightful share,” Khan said. The committee also thanked supporters and the media for highlighting the concerns of the people of Ramban and reiterated its resolve to continue pursuing the issues related to compensation, rehabilitation, employment and development benefits.

articles.title: Beyond Local Markets: How MSMEs Can Unlock Growth Through Exports and GeM
articles.description: New Delhi [India], September 10: MSMEs looking to scale can find growth beyond familiar markets. Exports can open doors to global customers, while the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) can connect businesses with institutional buyers across India.
